page: Amazon Web Services c9g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 cores using the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor model at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. With a 1:1 virtual-to-physical core configuration and no hyperthreading, each core operates independently with 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, supported by a shared 96 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 384.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, includes no hardware GPUs, and features no local NVMe storage, relying solely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate extreme multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth. In stress-ng evaluations, the multi-core CPU benchmark reached a top-tier score of 380,393.63, despite single-core performance falling into the median range at 2,006.19. Multi-threaded data decompression via bzip3 reached 1,910.26 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput measured 341.63 GB/sec. Memory read operations hit 729.09 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB blocks and write speeds reached 340.16 GB/sec, contributing to a top-tier PassMark memory score of 4,605.11 and 511.16 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 1:2 core-to-memory footprint and high physical core density make the c9g.48xlarge cost-efficient for massively parallel computational tasks that do not require x86 instruction sets or attached local disks. However, notable tradeoffs include the absence of integrated accelerators, which limits sequential generative LLM output (recording 12.87 tokens/sec on smaller 135M models), and the reliance on external storage for persistent persistence. It delivers optimal workload fit for high-concurrency batch processing, scientific simulations, distributed compilation, and highly scaled caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by 192 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores running at 3.3 GHz without hyperthreading. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, the system supplies 384.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and a 100 Gbps network interface, though it omits local storage and dedicated GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the c9g.48xlarge excels in multi-threaded execution, producing a top-tier stress-ng multi-core score of 380,393.63 and strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 729 GB/sec. Redis throughput exceeds 511 million operations per second, matching high-scale data needs. While its architecture presents lower single-core LLM text generation rates and lacks bundled storage, the instance maximizes resource density for compute-bound batch jobs, containerized microservices, scientific computing, and high-throughput network applications.
